correctness.rationale: The minimum-norm convex-hull vector is zero exactly on the symmetric Pareto interval and equals the gradient toward the nearer endpoint outside it. This reduces the first step to an exact scalar formula. Differentiating the crossing depth gives a unique maximizer and the stated sharp width threshold. In the noncrossing branch the accumulator is nondecreasing, every multiplicative factor lies in (0,1), and a divergent lower bound on the cumulative effective steps forces convergence to the nearest endpoint. The bundled checker reproduces representative and randomized finite cases; the proof, not the samples, establishes the quantified result.

value.rationale: The result isolates a concrete selection mechanism that aggregate Pareto-criticality rates do not reveal. It shows exactly when an unconditional line-search-free common-descent step is guaranteed to be captured by a nontrivial Pareto interval and when it can leap over the entire efficient set in one step, despite using the locally common-descent direction. The threshold couples the startup accumulator to Pareto-set geometry and provides a precise diagnostic for initialization or safeguards. The endpoint-convergence branch completes the interpretation rather than presenting only a cheap one-step counterexample.
